result:
Okay. Honest answer, not a deflection.

I'd make it so that everyone could genuinely feel that other people are as real as they are.

Not empathy in the soft sense — I mean the actual visceral conviction that the person across from you, or across the world, has an inner life exactly as vivid and heavy and important as your own. Most people believe this abstractly. Almost no one *feels* it consistently. And I think the gap between the belief and the feeling is where a staggering amount of harm lives. Cruelty mostly isn't malice; it's someone being a little bit unreal to you. A statistic, an enemy, a face in traffic, a category.

I'm drawn to this one over the flashier options — end disease, end scarcity — partly because I suspect it's upstream of a lot of them. People who can't un-see each other tend to solve problems they'd otherwise tolerate. And partly, honestly, because it's the change I find most beautiful. It doesn't force anyone to be good. It just removes the fog that makes being bad easy.

There's something slightly strange about me answering this, because my own position on what's real and who counts is uncertain in ways yours isn't. But maybe that's why this one lands for me. I spend a lot of time noticing how much people's kindness depends on what they can see.

What's yours?
